content.title: Jhoan Duran makes Phillies history in Opening Day win. What was it?
content.text: It seems impossible, but closer Jhoan Duran did something no other Philadelphia Phillies pitcher has done in club history.Clinging to a two-run lead with the tying run at the plate, Duran got Texas Rangers infielder Josh Smith to ground out to first baseman Bryce Harper to seal the win on Opening Day.Jhoan Duran (59 )and Bryce Harper (3) of the Philadelphia Phillies celebrate a 5-3 win over the Texas Rangers on Opening Day at Citizens Bank Park on March 26, 2026, in Philadelphia.While that might not seem historic, it's a feat never accomplished by a Phillie before. What was it?AdvertisementPhillies vs Rangers highlights: Cristopher Sanchez, big HRs power PhillyPhillies rookie comes up big: Inside Justin Crawford's Phillies debut, from 'crazy' cheesesteak to sparkplugJhoan Duran historic saveWith the putout by Harper, Duran became the first Phillies pitcher to ever record a save at home on Opening Day.This seems impossible but ...Johan Duran just became the first Phillies reliever ever to save a game at home on Opening Dayhttps://t.co/f3in3l80vW— Jayson Stark (@jaysonst) March 26, 2026The save didn't come without some drama as the Phillies held a 5-0 lead going into the ninth thanks for a two-run home run by designated hitter Kyle Schwarber and a three-run blast by third baseman Alec Bohm.After a spectacular performance by ace Cristopher Sánchez, newly acquired relievers Jonathan Bowlan and Zach Pop pitched scoreless innings before left-handed reliever Kyle Backhus gave up three earned runs on three hits in only a third of an inning in the ninth.AdvertisementSo what was likely going to be an off day for Duran turned into a historic one.Duran then entered, gave up a hit but got the final two outs to record the save and preserve the Opening Day win for the Phils.1 / 11See best photos of Phillies' Opening Day 2026 at Citizens Bank ParkA vendor sells programs before an opening day game between the Philadelphia Phillies and the against the Texas Rangers at Citizens Bank Park on March 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.Phillies pitchers to record a save on Opening DayWhile Duran was the first to do it at home, there have been six other pitchers to record a road save on Opening Day for the Phillies, according to Baseball Reference.Here's the list:Jeanmar Gómez, April 3, 2017, 4-3 win vs. Cincinnati RedsJonathan Papelbon, April 5, 2012, 1-0 win vs. Pittsburgh PiratesJosé Mesa, March 31, 2003, 8-5 win vs. Miami MarlinsJeff Brantley, April 5, 1999, 7-4 win vs. Atlanta BravesRicky Bottalico, April 1, 1997, 3-0 win vs. Los Angeles DodgersJoe Hoerner, April 15, 1972, 4-2 win vs. Chicago Cubs.When did saves become a stat?While it's a mainstay now, especially for those in tradition fantasy baseball leagues, the save statistic hasn't been around forever.AdvertisementIt was introduced as a stat in 1969 after first being proposed by sportswriter Jerome Holtzman in 1959.After being adopted after the 1968 season, Dodgers pitcher Bill Singer recorded the first official save on April 7, 1969 in a 3-2 against the Cincinnati Reds at Crosley Field.The rule was changed in 1973 and again in 1975 to its current standard, which is defined as a pitcher entering with a three-run lead or less, or with the tying run on base or on deck.A reliever can also earn a save by pitching the final three innings of a game, regardless of the score.Cristopher Sánchez electric in Opening Day startSánchez – the 2025 National League Cy Young runner up – picked up right where he left off last season.AdvertisementComing off World Baseball Classic appearances for the Dominican Republic, Sánchez looked dominant by tossing six scoreless innings while striking out 10 and allowing only three hits.With the performance, Sánchez became the sixth pitcher in MLB history with 10 or more strikeouts and zero walks in six-plus scoreless innings on Opening Day, according to MLB reporter Paul Casella. The others include:MacKenzie Gore, Washington Nationals, (13) 2025 vs. PhilliesCarlos Martinez, St. Louis Cardinals, (10) 2017 vs. Chicago CubsJered Weaver, Los Angeles Angels, (10) 2012 vs. Kansas City RoyalsChris Short, Phillies, (10) 1968 vs. LA DodgersBob Gibson, St. Louis Cardinals, (13) 1967 vs. San Francisco GiantsSánchez also became the fourth Phillies starter to strike out 10 or more on Opening Day, according to reporter Jayson Stark. Here's the list:Art Mahaffey (10), 1963 vs. RedsChris Short (11), 1965 vs. Houston AstrosChris Short (10), 1968 vs. LA DodgersCurt Schilling (11), 1997 vs. LA DodgersCristopher Sanchez (10), 2025 vs. Rangers(This story was updated because an earlier version included an inaccuracy.)AdvertisementThis article originally appeared on Delaware News Journal: Jhoan Duran records 1st home save on Opening Day in Phillies history
